comments.author: fisj
comments.body: Can you at least explain what your game is. how you used AI in it? Right now this is a low effort post. See rule #6.

replies.author: SneakerHunterDev
replies.body: Yes my game is fully AI native. All Content is created by Players typing prompts and the game generates the content on the fly. Prompt a character, prompt a car, prompt a weapon, even prompt a City and it will appear in the online Universe. I want to create gta online but PLAYERS ARE the IP.

replies.author: ThinkingOutLoud-7742
replies.body: This sounds very much in the idea stage. If you’re gonna use prompts I’m assuming you’re gonna need enterprise subscriptions to some LLM agent which will be costly. So your game needs to generate enough players and revenue to offset that and turn a profit. Even if you don’t subscribe to an LLM and you have your generation methods, you’ll still need somewhere to host the instances because I’m assuming you’ll want concurrent player requests to be handled with little latency. That brings up another issue which is that generation introduces a lot of latency. Will people want to play a game where you can generate anything but it takes 30+ seconds to appear? I wouldn’t. If you can make it work then by all means. But these are problems that you’ll have to consider. If you don’t create something that feels seamless and easy, then what’s the difference between creating things in your game vs creating their own game with Claude? At that point it’s more like an AI game engine, which could be a good pivot.

replies.author: SneakerHunterDev
